name: second-reveal-still-carries-the-sidebar
description: The reporter sees an EMPTY panel. The first reveal draws the sidebar (edge-reveal-control's revealed frame proves it), so the suspect is the handover: docking hands the WebContents back to the pane, and the next reveal has to take it again. This reveals, dismisses, reveals a second time and grades the second panel against the first. A second reveal that comes up blank reads as no change from the hidden strip.

actions.note: first paint, and the sidebar announces itself
collapse the pane, which is the state the edge zone arms in
the baseline both reveals are graded against
the left window edge, where the reveal is armed
leave the edge, so the panel slides away and the pane takes its contents back
longer than the 240ms slide, so the dock-back has certainly run
the frame the reporter says is empty

assertions.label: the-first-reveal-carries-the-sidebar
assertions.desc: The control half. If this fails the run says nothing about the second reveal.

assertions.label: so-does-the-second
assertions.desc: The measurement. A panel that comes up empty reads the same as the hidden strip, so the delta collapses and this fails.
